result.markdown: --- title: "Discrete-time models" course-unit: ch02-discrete-time-models status: complete --- ## Why this unit matters - Epidemic data arrive in discrete intervals; many simulations advance in fixed steps. - Two flavours of discrete-time SIR: - a **deterministic function map** (continuous state); - a **stochastic Markov chain** (integer counts). - As $\delta t\to0$ the map converges to the continuous ODE — tying discrete and continuous worlds together. ## Equations {.smaller} Per-step probabilities (@eq-s-ch02-probs) from the SIR rates; the map moves expectations, the chain draws binomials: $$ p_I = 1-e^{-\beta c I_t \delta t/N},\quad p_R = 1-e^{-\gamma\delta t}. $$ {#eq-s-ch02-probs} $$ \text{map:}\;\; S_{t+1}=S_t-p_I S_t,\;\; I_{t+1}=I_t+p_I S_t-p_R I_t,\;\; R_{t+1}=R_t+p_R I_t. $$ {#eq-s-ch02-map} $$ \text{chain:}\;\; Y_t\sim\text{Bin}(S_t,p_I),\;\; Z_t\sim\text{Bin}(I_t,p_R). $$ {#eq-s-ch02-chain} The map is the mean-field expectation of the chain. ## Julia API: two kernels side by side ::: {#cell-s-ch02-kernels .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using Distributions, StableRNGs rate_to_proportion(r, δt) = -expm1(-r * δt) function map_step(state, p, δt) # deterministic S, I, R = state; β, c, γ, N = p inf = rate_to_proportion(β * c * I / N, δt) * S rec = rate_to_proportion(γ, δt) * I (S - inf, I + inf - rec, R + rec) end function chain_step(state, p, δt, rng) # stochastic S, I, R = state; β, c, γ, N = p Y = rand(rng, Binomial(round(Int, S), rate_to_proportion(β * c * I / N, δt))) Z = rand(rng, Binomial(round(Int, I), rate_to_proportion(γ, δt))) (S - Y, I + Y - Z, R + Z) end function iterate_model(step, u0, p, δt, n; extra = ()) traj = Matrix{Float64}(undef, 3, n + 1); traj[:, 1] .= u0; s = Tuple(float.(u0)) for k in 1:n; s = step(s, p, δt, extra...); traj[:, k+1] .= s; end traj end ``` ::: {#s-ch02-kernels .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` iterate_model (generic function with 1 method) ``` ::: ::: ## Generated result: map vs chain ::: {#cell-fig-s-ch02-compare .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using CairoMakie u0 = [990, 10, 0]; p = (0.05, 10.0, 0.25, 1000.0); δt = 1.0; n = 40; ts = 0:n mapt = iterate_model((s, p, dt) -> map_step(s, p, dt), u0, p, δt, n) nsims = 200 ens = [iterate_model(chain_step, u0, p, δt, n; extra = (StableRNG(seed),)) for seed in 1:nsims] chainI = reduce(hcat, (t[2, :] for t in ens)); meanI = vec(sum(chainI; dims = 2)) ./ nsims fig = Figure(size = (760, 380)); ax = Axis(fig[1,1]; xlabel = "day", ylabel = "I(t)") for j in 1:nsims; lines!(ax, ts, chainI[:, j]; color = (:grey, 0.1)); end lines!(ax, ts, meanI; color = :firebrick, linewidth = 3, label = "chain mean") lines!(ax, ts, mapt[2, :]; color = :black, linestyle = :dash, linewidth = 3, label = "map") axislegend(ax; position = :rt); fig ``` ::: {#fig-s-ch02-compare .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Infectious compartment: stochastic chain realisations (grey), their mean (red), and the deterministic map (dashed). The map tracks the stochastic mean. ::: ::: ## Validation: convergence to the ODE ::: {#cell-s-ch02-check .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using OrdinaryDiffEq function sir_ode!(du, u, p, t) S, I, R = u; β, c, γ, N = p; λ = β * c * I / N du[1] = -λ * S; du[2] = λ * S - γ * I; du[3] = γ * I; return nothing end ref = solve(ODEProblem(sir_ode!, float.(u0), (0.0, 40.0), p), Tsit5(); reltol = 1e-12, abstol = 1e-12, save_everystep = false).u[end] δts = [40.0 / 2^k for k in 5:12] errs = map(δts) do dt m = iterate_model((s, p, d) -> map_step(s, p, d), u0, p, dt, round(Int, 40.0 / dt)) maximum(abs.(m[:, end] .- ref)) end order = sum(log2(errs[k] / errs[k+1]) for k in 1:length(errs)-1) / (length(errs) - 1) cons = all(k -> isapprox(sum(mapt[:, k]), 1000.0; atol = 1e-8), 1:n+1) (round(order; digits = 3), isapprox(order, 1.0; atol = 0.1), cons) ``` ::: {#s-ch02-check .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.96, true, true) ``` ::: ::: First-order convergence and conservation confirmed. ## Limitations & takeaways - The **chain** is most faithful: integer counts, chance extinction, run-to-run variability shrinking with population size. - The **map** is its cheap, smooth mean-field shadow — blind to fluctuations. - Both are exact only as $\delta t\to0$; a within-step artefact (no infect *and* recover in one step) vanishes as the step shrinks. - **Takeaway:** discrete models bridge data cadence and continuous theory. ::: {.notes} Stress that the map is literally the expectation of the chain's update, which is why the red mean and dashed map coincide. The convergence study reuses the forward-Euler order analysis from the calculus prerequisite. Encourage learners to shrink δt in the notebook and watch both the discretisation error and the extinction probability change. ::: ## Learn more - Book chapter: [Discrete-time models](../../chapters/02-discrete-time-models.html) - Pluto notebook: [`02-discrete-time-models.jl`](../../notebooks/chapters/02-discrete-time-models.jl) - [Distributions.jl](https://juliastats.org/Distributions.jl/stable/)
